mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a strong labor market, which is typically associated with economic growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns when UNRATE is below 4.5%, more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 1.5%, it may indicate monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows positive 20-day returns more than 40% of the time when FEDFUNDS exceeds 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) coupled with increasing federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by 0.5% and FEDFUNDS increases by 0.25%
failure_condition: The S&P 500 does not show negative returns 60 days after both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS increase as specified.

mechanism_narrative: Positive GDP growth (GDPC1) indicates strong economic demand, which should drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns when GDPC1 indicates positive growth, more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals strong labor market conditions, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 does not show positive 5-day returns after PAYEMS increases by 50,000, more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth (GDPC1) combined with rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicates economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth rate decreases and UNRATE increases by 0.2%
failure_condition: The S&P 500 does not show negative returns 60 days after GDPC1 and UNRATE changes as specified.

mechanism_narrative: During a late-cycle expansion, an increase in industrial production (INDPRO) may not prevent an eventual economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns when INDPRO increases during a late-cycle expansion, more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong demand in the housing market, which is typically associated with positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns when HOUST increases, more than 45% of the time.
